texts.facts: This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.200,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.10.2023 at about 8.00am. 2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that: On 09.10.2023 at about 8.00am the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-HY- 5657 from Kodigehalli to Hoodi Main Road near SJR Phase 2 layout, a TATA Ace Mega XL bearing No.KA- 53-D-1018 which was parked near Nandini Milk Parlour for unloading the goods without following any safety measures, all of a sudden the driver of the said vehicle without showing any hand signal or any gestures, he getting out of the vehicle has opened the right side of the vehicle's door i.e., the Driver's side Door. Due to forceful opening of the door which hit the petitioner's motorcycle. Due to impact, the petitioner fell down on the ground and sustained injuries. Immediately, he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, near ITPL Road, Shantinekethan, provided first aid and MLC was done and thereafter referred to a Surgeon , the surgeon who addressed the petitioner said that it was worse the bone of Index Finger is broken and he had to undergo an anaesthetic surgery. Thereafter the petitioner was admitted at Manipla Hospital, underwent surgery and discharged on 10.10.2023 with advice to take rest. So far he has spent huge amount towards medical, hospital charges, medicines, attendant charges, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses. Due to the said accidental injuries, he could not do his normal work as previous and could not attend the office and lost salary. Prajwal U vs Anil V on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157221820/ 2 3. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as an Advocate and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family. The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent by the driver of the parked Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-D-1018 and KR Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.347/2023 p/u/Secs.283 & 338 of IPC and 134 (a & b), 187, 146, 196, 56, 192 of MV Act. The respondents being the RC owner and the Driver of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition. 4. In response to the service of summons, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement. In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte. 4A. The respondent No.2 has denied the entire petition averments. Further denied the manner of accident, injuries suffered by the petitioner. He further denied the medical expenses incurred by him. The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself. He dashed himself to the lorry in a rash and negligent manner and contributing to the alleged accident. Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against him. 6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Twenty-Four documents as Exs.P1 to P24. The respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
texts.arguments: The petitioner has also produced final bill at Ex.P.16 for Rs.99,885/- of Manipal Hospital and The petitioner has produced the out patient bills and vehicle repair invoice for Rs.17,406/-. The discharge summary shows that the petitioner has taken treatment at Manipal Hospital from 09.10.2023 to 10.10.2023 for 2 days. The petitioner has produced the out patient bills and vehicle repair invoice.
